response.sql:
WITH fee_with_net_rate AS (
  SELECT
    orderslink,
    rebtotal,
    (feerate - rebrate) AS net_fee_rate
  FROM fees
),
order_stats AS (
  SELECT
    orderslink,
    AVG(rebtotal) AS avg_rebtotal,
    AVG(net_fee_rate) AS avg_net_fee_rate
  FROM fee_with_net_rate
  WHERE orderslink IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY orderslink
),
benchmark AS (
  SELECT AVG(net_fee_rate) AS benchmark_rate
  FROM fee_with_net_rate
  WHERE orderslink IS NOT NULL
),
filtered_orders AS (
  SELECT
    os.avg_rebtotal,
    os.avg_net_fee_rate,
    (os.avg_net_fee_rate - b.benchmark_rate) AS excess_rate
  FROM order_stats os
  CROSS JOIN benchmark b
  WHERE os.avg_net_fee_rate > b.benchmark_rate
)
SELECT
  AVG(avg_rebtotal) AS avg_of_avg_rebates,
  AVG(avg_net_fee_rate) AS avg_of_avg_net_fees,
  AVG(excess_rate) AS avg_excess_over_benchmark
FROM filtered_orders;

assumptions.assumption: The benchmark net fee rate is calculated from fee records belonging to orders (non-NULL orderslink) only, not including fee records with no associated order. This aligns with the context that orders count "once for each fee record it has" and keeps the benchmark consistent with the population being compared.

alternatives.interpretation: The benchmark is calculated from all fee records in the dataset, including those with NULL orderslink. The phrase "all fee records directly" is interpreted literally without filtering.
